text:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's calibration pass on the 13B mix-precision pipeline we saw a ~35% throughput regression in the nightly perf job when switching between FP8 and INT8 kernels. I think it's tied to kernel handoff + KV cache invalidation during long-prefix batches. Anyone else see this?
jon: hm, do you have the profiler traces? Is it the kernel selection branching or something else (e.g. memory copies)?
maya: I pulled a flamegraph for the failing run. Key points: kernel selector spends <10ms deciding, but there are repeated KV cache misses right after the handoff. Throughput went from ~280 toks/s to ~180 toks/s for the same batch distribution.
lee: can you paste the hot stack? Also what batching heuristic are you using? continuous batching or fixed window?
maya: continuous batching w/ dynamic batch-size cap=48, seq-dist cutoff=1024. The handoff happens when an input's effective precision policy flips mid-request due to kv-length estimate. Flame:
```
hot path: attention_kernel_fp8 -> copy_kv_to_fp8_workspace -> kv_rebuild -> attention_kernel_int8 -> kv_miss_handler
wall times: copy_kv 12.3ms, kv_rebuild 18.7ms, attention_int8 9.1ms
```
jon: kv_rebuild 18.7ms is the culprit. Why are we rebuilding the KV for the same request? Should be shared between kernel variants if shapes match.
sophia: reminds me of the calibration artifacts. If calibration produced per-channel scaling with different layout assumptions, kernels don't consider them compatible and force a rebuild. Are we doing per-channel quant scales for keys/values?
maya: yes — we switched to per-channel for better accuracy on the head layers. My suspicion: per-channel quant for KV means workspace/offload layout shifts and runtime can't reuse the cached buffers, so it rebuilds.
lee: interesting. That would explain both increased CPU and extra copies. Do we have an experiment comparing per-tensor vs per-channel kv quant for perf?
sophia: accuracy-wise per-channel wins on outlier-heavy heads, but it is fragile to tail samples. If our calibration dataset contains rare long-tail tokens/strings, scales blow up and kernels choose different quant params. I suggested median-based clipping in the last meeting to dampen that.
kai: FYI the autoscaler noticed the spike and triggered a scale-up; cost implications here are non-trivial. We should avoid unpredictable perf swings.
jon: proposed repro steps: 1) run the nightly perf harness with forced per-tensor quant for KV, 2) run with per-channel + sample-trim(0.5pct), 3) run with per-channel + median-clipping rule. Compare throughput and latency P95.
maya: I ran 1) already — throughput stayed ~275 toks/s and no kv_rebuild. So per-tensor is much cheaper operationally. But quality delta is visible for some QA prompts.
sophia: can you share the calibration sampling config? I think outlier weighting matters a lot.
maya: current sampler:
```json
{"dataset":"webmix-2025","samples":50000,"sample_strategy":"random_stratified","tail_fraction":0.02}
```
We included full tails for coverage. That might be the problem.
sophia: yeah 2% tail is large; tail samples disproportionately influence per-channel scales. I prefer a winsorized approach: cap per-sample contribution at the 95th percentile, or use Huber loss when fitting scales.
lee: can we get profiling numbers for a small synthetic: 10k requests with long prefix (>4096), comparing: A) per-tensor, B) per-channel raw tail, C) per-channel + winsorize. If we see kv_rebuilds only in B then decision is clear.
kai: also add a run that forces kernel-compatibility flag that lets different quant params share buffers if quant type and shape match — might be safer short-term.
jon: we should be careful: forcing compatibility could mask correctness issues. Need strict validation harness for logits/outputs. But it's a good perf experiment.
maya: I attached the perf logs (summarized):
- baseline per-tensor: throughput 276 toks/s, kv_rebuilds 2 per 10k reqs
- per-channel raw: throughput 176 toks/s, kv_rebuilds 218 per 10k reqs
- per-channel + winsorize: throughput 265 toks/s, kv_rebuilds 8 per 10k reqs
So winsorize recovers almost all perf.
sophia: those numbers line up with the hypothesis. Any quality deltas on eval suite?
maya: eval rouge/accuracy: per-channel raw is +0.9% on some doc summarization sets vs per-tensor, winsorize is +0.6%. Margin may be acceptable for production if winsorize avoids perf collapse.
lee: nice. For kernels, do we have a fast path to detect when quant params are compatible? A small checksum of scale arrays could be cached and compared cheaply before deciding to rebuild. If identical or extremely close within eps, reuse the buffers.
jon: agreed — store a 64-bit hash of quant params per-layer + shape/version. If mismatch, and l2-diff < eps threshold, skip rebuild. Risk: small difference may still change numeric results slightly. Must gate behind a flag and run numerical drift tests.
kai: I can add the flag to runtime; let's default it off for canaries. We should also add telemetry: count of forced-shares vs actual-rebuilds and avg kv_rebuild_time.
sophia: on the calibration side, propose updating sampling policy to: stratified samples across lengths + 0.5% tail cap + winsorize at 95th percentile per-layer. Document rationale.
maya: I'll open a PR for the sampler change and include the perf experiment logs. Also will add the kernel-compatibility flag patch for canary.
jon: ok next steps: maya PR + lee will run the 10k synthetic with the new flag on canary machines, sophia will add the winsorize option to calibration pipeline, kai will wire telemetry, and we'll reconvene after results.
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: maya/calib-winsorize + jon/kernel-compat-flag -> canary cluster in 2h :rocket:
maya: thanks everyone. If winsorize keeps quality within 0.5% and perf stable, we'll default to winsorized per-channel for the head layers only and fall back to per-tensor for deeper layers. Sounds reasonable?
sophia: sounds good to me. :+1:
lee: SGTM. I'll add a perf dashboard panel for kv_rebuild rate.
kai: adding alert on kv_rebuild_rate > 50/min for primary clusters.
maya: closing the loop — I'll paste the PR link when ready. Thanks. :pray:
